results.title: Subscribe to Reports and Dashboards (Lightning Experience) | Salesforce
results.content: Get the latest Salesforce data in picture-perfect format by subscribing to reports and dashboards in Lightning Experience. It’s time for the Monday 9AM sales meeting. In the past, it’s been a weekly fire drill to update your pipeline dashboards before the meeting. No longer! By subscribing to a dashboard, you can have it refreshed and waiting in your email inbox when you arrive at work. You can even have the same dashboards delivered to selected teammates. Here’s how to subscribe yourself and others to a dashboard. You can also subscribe to reports from the Reports tab. Find the dashboard you want to subscribe to and click the More Actions arrow, then Subscribe. Or, open the dashboard, and then click Subscribe. Notice the two main Edit Subscription sections. Under Schedule, set when you [...] Edit Subscription sections. Under Schedule, set when you want to refresh and email the dashboard. Under Email Results, choose who you want to receive the refreshed dashboard results by email. First let’s set the schedule. To be ready for Monday morning, select Weekly for the frequency and Monday for the day. To have enough time to review the results before 9am, let’s set the time to 8am. Now let’s choose who will receive the dashboard each week. ‘Me’ is the default, which means that you’re on the list. But what about your teammate who will be covering for you when you’re out of town next week? To include your teammate, search for her using the Select People option. After adding one or more recipients, click Save. You’re now back on the Dashboard tab, where you can see that you’ve set up a [...] the Dashboard tab, where you can see that you’ve set up a subscription. By sorting on the Subscribe column, you can see all the dashboards that you’ve subscribed to. Want to subscribe to a report instead? No problem. The process is exactly the same as for dashboards. And what about unsubscribing, if you no longer want to have the dashboard or report delivered? In the same Edit Subscription modal, you can remove any individual subscribers, or click Unsubscribe to unsubscribe everyone. By the way, dashboard subscription emails look great on a mobile device. That’s dashboard and report subscriptions in a nutshell. For more information see these topics in Salesforce Help. Or join us on the trail at trailblazer. salesforce.com

results.title: Subscriptions - Docs - PostHog
results.content:
The subscriptions page shows a paginated table of all subscriptions across your dashboards and insights. You can use tabs to filter by All subscriptions, My subscriptions, Dashboard, or Insight.

From here you can:

 Search for subscriptions by name
 Filter by delivery channel (email or Slack) and creator
 Sort by creation date, next delivery date, title, or creator
 Edit a subscription by navigating to its source insight or dashboard
 Test delivery to immediately send a subscription without waiting for the next scheduled delivery
 Delete subscriptions with an undo option

## Creating a subscription

To create a subscription, click Subscribe in the sidebar of any insight or dashboard.

New Subscription ButtonNew Subscription Button

## Selecting insights for dashboard subscriptions [...] ### When AI credits run out

If your organization exhausts its AI credit budget, subscriptions with AI summaries will still deliver on schedule, but without the AI-generated summary:

 The subscription delivers as normal with your insights or dashboard
 The AI summary is skipped for that delivery
 No notification is sent since the subscription itself continues to function
 Once credits are available again, AI summaries automatically resume

This is different from prompt subscriptions which pause entirely when credits run out, and from disabled subscriptions which require manual intervention.

## Prompt subscriptions [...] ### 3. Creating a new Slack subscription in PostHog

After installing the app, head back to PostHog and add a new subscription. You can do this in any dashboard or insight by clicking Subscribe in the sidebar, and then Add subscription.

Add to Slack buttonAdd to Slack button

You can then select any channel the app has access to and set a frequency. Private channels are only listed if you have already added PostHog to the relevant channel.

Slack channel selectionSlack channel selection

After you share a dashboard, you can notify users of updates by automatically emailing the
latest version on a schedule you configure. In this article, you'll learn to email dashboards
to other agents, admins, and groups. On Enterprise plans, you can also email dashboards to end users.

This article contains the following topics: [...] Explore dashboard delivery schedule

Note that the scheduled time isn’t exactly
the same as the delivery time. The scheduled time of a dashboard is the point
in time at which the dashboard’s reports are calculated using the data that's
currently synced in Explore. Meaning, if you schedule a dashboard for 9 AM,
recipients might not get the dashboard until sometime after 9 AM, but the reports
they see when they do get the dashboard will reflect the data that existed in
Explore as of 9 AM.

For complex reports or large sets of data, it might take
some time for the data to be calculated and sent before the dashboard reaches
recipients. [...] The person who created the
schedule and all Explore admins will receive two reminders when your schedule is
nearing expiration: one week before and one day before the expiration date.

If you're using Explore Enterprise and want to schedule dashboard
deliveries to end users, you must first enable this for each user by adding the
explore tag to their user profile. For details, see Scheduling dashboard deliveries with end users.

You
cannot schedule dashboards to users with Limited viewer and Limited editor permissions.

The schedule you configured is displayed on the Scheduled deliveries page.

Recipients of scheduled deliveries are grouped by language and time zone, with one email
sent to each group.
